svg.text: 01 · The sound desk: Cues (desktop, 1280 px)
Replaces mockup 12’s one-page console. The page splits into four sub-pages under one master strip. Book shots O9, O11, O12.

Mute all 15 min
Sound check sent to every zone at 21:31:40.
Main hall played it · Entrance has no sound screen, so nothing was heard there.
What changed and why
Four sub-pages, one master strip
O9 was one 7,000 px page: budget, master,
categories, 25 cues, library and log in a
row. Now Cues, Library, Limits and categories
and Log are sub-pages; the strip with the
master sits on top of each.
The master is a slider; mute and check stay one tap
Master volume is a slider with its value, not
a number box. Mute all 15 min and Sound check
(with its zone menu) sit at the right of the
strip, so the crew finds them on every
sub-page (O11, O12).
Plain names first
Each cue reads as what it is, "Urgent
announcement"; its id and sounds are the grey
second line. O9 listed raw ids such as
announce.urgent as links.
Levels as bars
A cue’s level is a bar with its percent, and
the slider is in the editor. Typed level
boxes are gone from the list.
Preview in place
The round play button plays the cue’s sound
and its picture on the virtual screen,
without opening it.
Grouped and filtered by category
Cues group under their category, with its
level and calm rule beside the heading; chips
filter, search finds by name or id. New cue
is the one primary action.
The row opens the editor
The whole row is the link (sheet 02); On is a
switch in the row.
Fits 1280 px
O9 was 1,291 px wide at 1280. No table here
is wider than the content column; the long
lists are rows, not table columns.
